content: The benefits of taking this medication are considered to outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. In the United States, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, in Canada, contact your doctor for guidance on side effects. Precautions: Before taking mefloquine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to quinine, or to quinidine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Mefloquine may cause dizziness or balance problems. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Mefloquine may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Mefloquine passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of mefloquine from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Long-Term Use: If you are taking this medication for an extended period, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as eye exams and liver function tests) should be conducted regularly. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Warning: Mefloquine may cause mental, mood, or nervous system problems. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience serious side effects such as mental or mood changes (e.g., anxiety, depression, restlessness, confusion, hallucinations, suicidal thoughts or attempts), ringing in the ears, dizziness, lightheadedness, loss of balance, or trouble sleeping. These side effects may persist even after stopping mefloquine, and some (e.g., dizziness, ringing in the ears, loss of balance) may become permanent. How to Use: Read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist before starting mefloquine and each time you get a refill. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Take this medication by mouth as directed by your doctor. Take it with food or milk to prevent stomach upset. Do not take it on an empty stomach. Swallow each dose with a full glass (8 ounces or 240 milliliters) of water. Dosage for children is based on weight. Early vomiting may occur in children after taking mefloquine. If vomiting occurs, contact your doctor immediately to determine if another dose is needed. When using this medication to prevent malaria, it is typically taken once a week. Take it as prescribed for the full course of treatment. It is crucial not to miss any doses and to take the drug on a regular schedule. After returning from a malaria-endemic area, continue taking this medication for an additional four weeks. If this medication is being used for malaria prevention, understand that it is still possible to contract the disease. Notify your doctor immediately if you develop a fever. Common side effects may include stomach upset or pain, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, headache, muscle pain, or diarrhea. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for guidance.
